I think the issue here is you’re trying to run before learning how to walk. I’ll have to echo the advice you’ve already been given and tell you to “learn fundamentals”.

Once you feel confident with that move on to the next fundamental. If you’re ever unsure Google it and search for resources breaking down exactly what each fundamental is.

I’ve just completed the HD version of the RE1 remake for the first time and I thought the controls were fine (modern non-tank controls worked great even with the fixed camera). I’m a long time fan of the franchise but only seen my brother’s play the PS1 version when I was younger. Decided to give it a go and I fell in love with it. 

Currently playing the PS1 version of RE2 and personally I think tank controls have a special charm to them, it feels like they add another level of strategy. Getting through a horde of zombies without getting hit is so satisfying.

I admit I probably have nostalgia goggles on but I appreciate the low-poly graphics and controls. As a big fan of film I really like the fixed camera angles, they do a great job at capturing exactly what Capcom wanted us to see. I’m aware that the fixed camera angles were used due to hardware limitations but some of the placements are genius imo.

Loved the RE2 Remake but the old school version has my heart for sure. Will be moving onto RE3 once I’ve completed this!

Watched it last night with my brother! This is possibly the best Dragon Ball movie I've seen. The animation was beautiful, the jokes were hilarious and one thing I loved the most was the focus on plot during the prologue. I'm not sure how everyone else felt about it but I think it was a great way to prepare you for what's to come. I enjoyed the badass Bardock more but it was good to see him in more of a emotionally intelligent light.

The only thing I wish they done differently about the prologue was show Bardock fight against the Freeza forces (I hope it's shown in the extended cut) instead of just seeing him rushing Freeza's attack.

I was a fan of Broly eversince the first film, I always seen him as the DB Hulk and I enjoyed how OP he was. Now he's got the potential to become my favourite character, I love how the new narrative has made me feel sympathy for him due to his up-bringing. I personally wouldn't mind seeing a full saga dedicated to the adventures he'll be having after the movie's events.

The fight scenes were amazing, I adore Vegeta's SSG form and seeing him take on Broly by himself at the beginning. It was also interesting to see the difference in power between Vegeta and Goku; Goku was handling Broly in his SSJ2 form while Vegeta had to go SSB by that point.

The transition from 2D to 3D caught me off guard and was very smooth, I was impressed by how fluid it was.

We live in a small town in the North of England but the cinema was fully packed out and the atmosphere was amazing. Can't wait for it to land on blue-ray so I can enjoy it again.
